about: ges, boss, and grasp with missing="em" at ebic_gamma=0.0 against Tetrad 8.0.0's FGES, BOSS, and GRaSP under its EM covariance policy, and against Tetrad's test-wise deletion, that arm with its effective sample size at the mean pairwise count, test-wise PC, listwise deletion, mean imputation, the complete-data fits of both packages, and the empty graph. Andrey's EM arms run the alternating structural EM; every other arm is the fit recorded with the earlier scheme, whose verdicts and rows are under earlier_scheme
build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (version string 0.16.0) with the alternating structural EM
scheme: alternating structural EM (Friedman, 1997): 10 searches, with 5 parameter-only EM steps on the current graph before each search after the first

references.ges(missing=\"em\"), boss(missing=\"em\": tetrad-lib 8.0.0, Java 21: FGES, BOSS, GRaSP with SemBicScore under MissingDataPolicy.EM_COVARIANCE at MissingDataSpec.of defaults (ridge 0, tolerance 1e-6, 1,000 iterations, FULL_N), penaltyDiscount 1.0; a one-pass EM estimate of a saturated covariance followed by the search, not structural EM; a second arm of it sets essMode to MEAN_PAIRWISE, the BIC's sample size being the mean over variable pairs of the rows where both are observed

verdict_rule: per cell and search: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs are not judged. A worse row counts only when the same cell on 20 fresh seeds is worse too. Floor: the interval of SHD(Andrey) - SHD(empty graph) must lie below 0; it decides a judged row at 15 variables and 100 rows where the reference's own interval lies below 0, and is reported elsewhere. A search passes a reference when no judged row is worse again and no judged row fails the floor. Its status is supported when it passes both references, the EM arm at FULL_N and at MEAN_PAIRWISE, and experimental otherwise.

ges(missing=\"em\").limit: at the plain BIC on Erdos-Renyi graphs of mean degree 4 the result is rarely better than the empty graph (3 of 54 cells); on the complete data the plain search's mean SHD is at or above the empty graph's in 4 of those 9 settings; at mean degree 2 it is below the empty graph in 50 of 54 cells

fresh_seeds.about: the first reference (FULL_N): no row is worse than it, so none ran again; the worse rows against test-wise PC, a baseline, were not rerun. The rows worse than the second reference are under second_reference.fresh_seed_reruns

second_reference.about: Tetrad's EM arm again with its effective sample size set to the mean pairwise count (MissingDataSpec.EffectiveSampleSizeMode.MEAN_PAIRWISE: the mean, over variable pairs, of the number of rows on which both variables are observed), on the same 2,640 masked datasets. Judged by the same rule as the first reference, and it counts for the status as the first does.

fresh_seed_reruns.about: the cells where Andrey's EM arm is worse than this arm, fit again on 20 fresh datasets each (seeds 20 to 39): Andrey's EM arm, this arm, and the empty graph. A cell is worse again when it is worse on both blocks. Tetrad's fits on the fresh datasets of three of the four cells are the ones recorded with the earlier scheme's reruns; the fourth cell was fit.

against_earlier_scheme.about: the alternating scheme against the earlier one, Andrey's EM arm of each search paired on the 20 datasets of a cell: D = SHD(alternating) - SHD(one refit per round), judged by the verdict rule. The cells where the alternating scheme is worse were not rerun on fresh seeds; in none of them is it worse than a reference arm on both seed blocks.

last_round_changed.about: fits of Andrey's EM arm whose last round returned another graph than the round before (metadata['em']['graph_changed'][-1]), which log a warning; by_size keys are variables x rows, values [fits whose last round changed the graph, fits]

fit_time_over_earlier_scheme.about: fit time of Andrey's EM arm, alternating over one refit per round, per dataset; the two were fit on different nodes at different times, so single ratios carry the noise of shared nodes; by_size keys are variables x rows

control_replication.about: the four settings where Andrey's plain search was worse than Tetrad's on the complete data on seeds 0 to 19, fit again on 20 fresh datasets each (seeds 20 to 39): the two packages' plain searches at the plain BIC and the empty graph, the same arms and settings as the control of the lane. A difference repeats when it is worse on both blocks.

refits.about: fits that failed on a read of the Python environment's files and were fit again; their records replace the failed ones. With the earlier scheme four (and a fifth, which never started, was run when its part resumed); in the reruns of Andrey's EM arms with the alternating scheme 13, and three more that never started were run when their parts resumed

earlier_scheme.about: the same lane with Andrey's EM arms as first measured, one refit per round: the verdicts that kept boss and grasp experimental, and every row. The other arms of its rows are the fits of the rows above.
earlier_scheme.build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (version string 0.16.0)
earlier_scheme.scheme: one refit per round: 10 searches, the graph's coefficients and noise variances fit once after each search
